mechanics.name: Bite the Bullet
mechanics.currentEffect: While healing yourself or another Survivor, suppress your Grunts of Pain and the sounds of the Healing action. Missing a Healing Skill Check creates no Loud Noise notification; instead it loses an additional 3/2/1% of total Healing progress.
activation: Begin a Healing action on yourself or another Survivor.
Ends/deactivates when: Sound suppression ends when the Healing action ends.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (unknown): No material live balance change could be verified from available patch history.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Healing becomes silent, and a missed Healing Skill Check costs extra progress instead of notifying the Killer.
specialInteractions: A missed Healing Skill Check has no Loud Noise notification; extra progress loss depends on tier.

editorial.summary: While healing yourself or someone else, suppress healing sounds and your Grunts of Pain; failed healing Skill Checks no longer alert the Killer and lose very little progress.
useCases: Hide a heal behind nearby cover while the Killer searches using sound.
Pair with Self-Care or other independent healing to create silent resets.
Reduce the punishment from missed healing Skill Checks.
counters: A Killer with direct vision or Aura reading can still find the heal.
Silent healing does not make the interaction faster.
Strong players rarely plan around missed Skill Checks.
pros: Completely removes important healing audio cues.
Works on self-heals and teammate heals.
Failed Skill Checks become much safer.
cons: Requires a situation where sound actually matters.
Can encourage slow hidden healing instead of productive objective play.
analysis: Bite the Bullet closes the top one hundred because silent healing can create clever escapes and resets, but it solves a narrower problem than the perks above it. Removing healing sounds and Grunts of Pain can make nearby searches surprisingly difficult when line of sight is already broken.
The perk pairs naturally with Self-Care and tracking-denial builds. A Killer may follow a trail into an area and expect to hear an injured Survivor healing, only to receive no useful sound cue.

The Skill Check protection is mostly insurance. Experienced players should not miss many standard healing checks, so the reduced progress loss and lack of a Loud Noise notification are helpful but not central to the ranking.

Bite the Bullet remains B because stealth healing can also become a tempo trap. Spending a long time hiding and healing silently is not automatically good play. The perk is best when silence changes a real Killer search, not when it merely makes a slow heal quieter.
editorial.verdict: A clever stealth-healing tool that can hide a reset under the Killer's nose. Bite the Bullet is useful, but silence alone does not make an inefficient heal efficient.
